name: issue_858_comfort_family_reactive_floor_breach
description: The comfort-family FSM must resolve a floor breach reactively, on the thermostatic temperature tick, without waiting for a second explicit classification cycle (Issue #858). Reproduces the live incident's shape: a warm day (native cooling), recency window cleared (cold-start engine, nothing recorded as recently cooling), indoor falls below comfort_heat -- the switch to heat must land within one sustain-confirm window of the first breach reading, driven purely by temp_update events.
notes: Occupant impact: on a live 2-zone install (Zone "Simulated 2"), indoor fell from 67F to
62F -- 6F below the 68F comfort floor -- over 2h40m overnight before heat engaged, because
the comfort-family FSM (Issue #827) only re-evaluated on apply_classification()'s ~30-minute
scheduled cycle. Unlike nat-vent (nat_vent_temperature_check()) and fan control
(fan_thermostat_check()), which already react to every current_temperature tick via
coordinator._async_thermostat_changed, the comfort-family defense had no equivalent.
Root cause investigation: a deterministic reproduction driving comfort_family_decision.py/
comfort_family_fsm.py directly with this incident's exact recorded values (67->66->65->64->
63->62F, floor=68, day_type=warm, 30-minute ticks, recency window already cleared) found NO
defect in that pure decision logic -- given a genuinely-cleared recency window, it already
resolves within one cycle. The fix is therefore to remove the up-to-30-minute ceiling on
when a cycle happens (comfort_family_temperature_check(), wired into
coordinator._async_thermostat_changed), not to change the decision math -- see
comfort_family_temperature_check()'s own docstring in automation.py.
This scenario proves the fix directly: only ONE classification event exists (at 06:00), and
the switch still lands by 06:17 -- driven entirely by temp_update events, which is only
possible because comfort_family_temperature_check() now re-enters apply_classification()
reactively. Before this fix, this exact event sequence would never switch at all within the
scenario's timeline (no second classification event ever fires to give the FSM another look).
Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md #10):
(a) Scenario effectiveness (revert-test): removing the coordinator._async_thermostat_changed
wiring (or the comfort_family_temperature_check() call it makes) makes this scenario
fail -- comfort_family_switch_by would never fire, since no classification event ever
re-runs apply_classification() in this event list.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md's automation logic table
gets a new row for this reactive-tick path, cross-referenced from the existing #827
deadband entries.
(c) Occupant experience: a person sleeping in a home whose indoor temperature drifts below
the comfort floor now gets heat within about a minute and a half of the drift being
detected, not up to 30 minutes (or, as in the live incident, several missed cycles and
hours) later.
Deliberately mirrors issue_827_hot_day_deadband_cleared_escalates.json's config/day-type
shape (comfort_heat=68, fan_mode disabled) so the only material difference is HOW the
sustain-confirm ticks are delivered -- classification events there, temp_update events here.

events.note: Warm-day classification (native cooling). Only classification event in this scenario -- everything after this is driven by temp_update alone.

First breach tick: 1F below comfort_heat(68). Cold-start engine -- nothing recorded as recently cooling, so the recency-gated deadband (Issue #843) is already 0F. comfort_family_temperature_check() fires reactively (indoor < band.floor), re-enters apply_classification() -- sustain-confirm candidate starts here, not yet confirmed (elapsed 0s < 90s).
120s after the first breach tick (>90s sustain window). Reactive check fires again, sustain-confirms, escalates to heating -- with no second classification event ever having run.

assertions.reason: Baseline: warm day, indoor within band -- comfort band arms normally at the ceiling.

Issue #858: the switch to heating lands by 06:17 -- 17 minutes after the scenario's only classification event, and 2 minutes after the first breach tick -- driven entirely by the reactive temperature-tick path, not a second scheduled classification cycle.
Final engine state confirms the family actually escalated, not just an emitted event.
The escalated mode is a real climate.set_temperature/set_hvac_mode call at comfort_heat, not merely an internal flag.

verdict.summary: A floor breach resolves to heat within one sustain-confirm window of the reactive temperature tick, without waiting for a second scheduled classification cycle (Issue #858).
verdict.observed_behavior: Single classification event at 06:00 (warm/cool), indoor drifts below the floor via temp_update alone at 06:15 and 06:17 -- comfort family escalates to heating by 06:17, driven entirely by the reactive tick.
verdict.expected_behavior: The comfort-family FSM must not depend on the ~30-minute apply_classification() cycle to notice a floor/ceiling breach -- every current_temperature tick must give it a chance to re-evaluate, matching nat-vent and fan control's existing reactivity.
